chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) should not touch anything of the perfume, nor from the Rihan (a type of fragrant herb), nor should he delight in it. So whoever is tested by something of that, let him give charity in proportion to what he did, in proportion to his satiety, meaning from the food.

key_terms.الرَّيْحَانِ: Rihan, a fragrant herb often used for scent
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.بِقَدْرِ شِبَعِهِ: In proportion to his satiety (amount of food eaten when full)
key_terms.يَتَلَذَّذُ: To delight or take pleasure in

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in Ihram who uses perfume?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, emphasizing that the prohibition extends beyond mere scent to include tactile contact and sensory delight in perfume or Rihan (a fragrant herb). The prescribed expiation, measured by the volume of food consumed when satiated, reflects the juristic principle of quantifying spiritual negligence through tangible material compensation, a method frequently discussed in Shia fiqh regarding Ihram violations.
